title: proxy.js
description: API reference for the proxy.js file.
related:
  title: Learn more about Proxy
  links:
    - app/api-reference/functions/next-request
    - app/api-reference/functions/next-response
---

> **Note**: The `middleware` file convention is deprecated and has been renamed to `proxy`. See [Migration to Proxy](#migration-to-proxy) for more details.

The `proxy.js|ts` file is used to write [Proxy](/docs/app/getting-started/proxy) and run code on the server before a request is completed. Then, based on the incoming request, you can modify the response by rewriting, redirecting, modifying the request or response headers, or responding directly.

Proxy executes before routes are rendered. It's particularly useful for implementing custom server-side logic like authentication, logging, or handling redirects.

> **Good to know**:
>
> Proxy is meant to be invoked separately of your render code and in optimized cases deployed to your CDN for fast redirect/rewrite handling, you should not attempt relying on shared modules or globals.
>
> To pass information from Proxy to your application, use [headers](#setting-headers), [cookies](#using-cookies), [rewrites](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/next-response#rewrite), [redirects](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/next-response#redirect), or the URL.

Create a `proxy.ts` (or `.js`) file in the project root, or inside `src` if applicable, so that it is located at the same level as `pages` or `app`.

If you’ve customized [`pageExtensions`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/pageExtensions), for example to `.page.ts` or `.page.js`, name your file `proxy.page.ts` or `proxy.page.js` accordingly.

```tsx filename="proxy.ts" switcher
import { NextResponse } from 'next/server'
import type { NextRequest } from 'next/server'

// This function can be marked `async` if using `await` inside
export function proxy(request: NextRequest) {
  return NextResponse.redirect(new URL('/home', request.url))
}

export const config = {
  matcher: '/about/:path*',
}
```

```js filename="proxy.js" switcher

}

export const config = {
  matcher: '/about/:path*',
}
```

## Exports

### Proxy function

The file must export a single function, either as a default export or named `proxy`. Note that multiple proxy from the same file are not supported.

content.text:
Email/password sign-up and sign-in, Google sign-in, and a protected `/dashboard` are all in place. I tested the password flow end to end against a dev server, but not Google.

What I tested:
- A signed-out request to `/dashboard` redirects to `/signin`.
- A wrong password is rejected.
- A newly created user could sign in and see the dashboard showing their own name.
- `tsc` passes apart from a `LayoutProps` error in `src/app/layout.tsx` that I didn't touch. Lint is clean.

I didn't run the sign-up form itself, only the underlying user-creation function plus sign-in. Google needs real credentials, so that path is untested.

**What I used.** Auth.js v5 (`next-auth@beta`) with signed-cookie sessions, plus `bcryptjs` for password hashing. I picked it because it handles Google and password sign-in in one library, and it supports Next 16. It's still a beta release.

**What changed**
- `src/lib/users.ts` now stores hashed passwords and has `createUserWithPassword`, `verifyPassword`, `upsertGoogleUser` and `getUserByEmail`. `getCurrentUser()` now reads the session instead of returning the first user. `listUsers`, `getUser` and the `User` type behave as before.
- `src/auth.ts` and `src/auth.config.ts` hold the Auth.js setup, and the auth route is at `src/app/api/auth/[...nextauth]/route.ts`.
- `src/proxy.ts` is the Next 16 replacement for middleware and guards `/dashboard`. The dashboard page also redirects if there's no user, as a second check.
- `/signin` and `/signup` are new pages, and the dashboard has a sign-out button.
- `.env.example` has placeholders for `AUTH_SECRET`, `AUTH_GOOGLE_ID` and `AUTH_GOOGLE_SECRET`. I added an exception to `.gitignore` so that file isn't ignored. Copy it to `.env.local` and fill it in. The Google redirect URI to register is `/api/auth/callback/google`.

**Things to know**
- **Storage:** the project has no database, so users still live in memory and reset on restart. The seed users (Ada, Grace) have no password, so they can't sign in with one. Swap the `users.ts` internals for real queries when you add a database.
- **Google accounts:** Google sign-in is refused unless Google reports the email as verified. If someone pre-registered that address with a password, signing in with Google removes that password. This stops them from keeping access to the real owner's account.
- **Sign-up:** a taken email shows a generic "can't be used, try signing in" message rather than saying the account exists.
- **Dev-server files:** running the dev server created `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` in the project. I deleted them because they aren't part of this change.
